title: An integral primitive element separating one valuation branch
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value $|\cdot|:F\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ (that is, $|a|=0$ exactly for $a=0$, $|ab|=|a||b|$, $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$, and some $a$ has $|a|\notin\{0,1\}$) [def-weil-field], and put $A=\{a\in F:|a|\leq1\}$, $\mathfrak m_A=\{a:|a|<1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $E/F$ be finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $C$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Suppose $C$ has precisely the finitely many distinct maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_r$, with $r\geq1$, and $C_{\mathfrak m_i}$ are valuation rings extending $A$. Suppose $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m_A\subseteq l=C/\mathfrak m_1$ is finite separable. Then there exists $x\in C$ with $E=F(x)$, whose residue $\bar x\in l$ is nonzero and generates $l$ over $\kappa$, and with $x\in\mathfrak m_i$ for every $i>1$. This includes $l=\kappa$ and $r=1$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1, converse proof, printed p. 11: choice of x_0 in the product of the other maximal ideals and primitive perturbation x=x_0+zy, with zy in every maximal ideal. Primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S2.SS2.

proof.text: Apply the primitive-element theorem to the assumed finite separable extension $l/\kappa$ to choose a generator $b$. If $l=\kappa$, choose $b=1$ instead. Otherwise a generator cannot be zero, since $\kappa(0)=\kappa$. Thus in either case $b\ne0$ and $l=\kappa(b)$. Distinct maximal ideals of $C$ are pairwise coprime: if $\mathfrak m_i+\mathfrak m_j$ were proper, maximality would force $\mathfrak m_j\subseteq\mathfrak m_i$, hence equality. The Chinese remainder isomorphism applied to this finite family, followed by taking a representative in $C$, gives $x_0$ with residue $b$ at $\mathfrak m_1$ and zero at every other $\mathfrak m_i$.

source.place: Tags 030N (fields-lemma-primitive-element) and 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder); applied to the stated residue extension and maximal ideals.

proof.text: Nontriviality supplies $t\in F$ with $0<|t|<1$: replace an element of absolute value greater than one by its inverse if necessary. In $A$, an element of absolute value one has its inverse in $A$, whereas an element of absolute value less than one cannot be a unit. The latter elements form the ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, so it is the unique maximal ideal. The extension $A\subset C$ is integral by the definition of $C$. Maximal contraction therefore gives $\mathfrak m_i\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$ for every $i$. In particular $t\in\mathfrak m_i$ for all $i$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1, converse proof, printed p. 11; primitive perturbation paragraph, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S2.SS2.; explicit elementary details supplied by Q131 (local PDF absent).

proof.text: Choose $y\in E$ with $E=F(y)$ by the primitive-element theorem. By separable algebraicity, $y$ has a monic polynomial $P(T)=T^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jT^j$ over $F$, with $d\ge1$. Fix an integer $N\ge0$ so large that $|a_j||t|^{N(d-j)}\le1$ for every $j<d$. Such an integer exists explicitly by taking $N\ge\max(0,\max_{j<d,\ a_j\ne0}\log|a_j|/((d-j)(-\log|t|)))$ and rounding up. The element $w=t^Ny$ satisfies the monic polynomial $T^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jt^{N(d-j)}T^j$ over $A$, obtained by multiplying $P(y)=0$ by $t^{Nd}$. Hence $w\in C$ by the definition of integral closure. Also $F(w)=F(y)=E$, since $t^N\in F^\times$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1, converse proof, printed p. 11; primitive perturbation paragraph, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S2.SS2.; explicit elementary details supplied by Q131 (local PDF absent).

proof.text: There are only finitely many proper intermediate fields $F\subseteq H\subsetneq E$. For each such $H$ at most one scalar $c\in F$ can satisfy $x_0+cw\in H$: if two distinct scalars $c,c'$ did, subtraction and division by $c-c'\in F^\times$ would give $w\in H$, contradicting $F(w)=E$. Thus there is a finite set $B\subset F$ outside of which $x_0+cw$ belongs to no proper intermediate field. For $c\notin B$, the intermediate field $F(x_0+cw)$ must consequently be $E$.

source.place: Tag 030N, fields-lemma-primitive-element, equivalence (1)--(2); elementary affine-line exclusion argument supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The scalars $t^n$, $n\ge1$, are pairwise distinct, because their absolute values $|t|^n$ strictly decrease. Choose $n\ge1$ with $t^n\notin B$ and set $x=x_0+t^nw$. Then $F(x)=E$ by the preceding step. As $w\in C$ and $t\in\mathfrak m_i$, the correction $t^nw$ lies in every $\mathfrak m_i$; it also lies in $C$, which is a subring. Therefore $x\in C$, its residue at $\mathfrak m_1$ is $b\ne0$, and $x\in\mathfrak m_i$ for every $i>1$. For $r=1$ the other congruences are empty, and when $E=F$ there are no proper intermediate fields to exclude. This proves all clauses.
